$comment: Planyr standing performance budgets (NEW-8). THESE ARE THE CEILING — a feature that
breaches one ships with a matching optimization, or does not ship. See docs/PERF-BUDGETS.md
for the rule, the measurement blockers, and how to change a number here.
THE BUNDLE METRICS CARRY A BASELINE, NOT A HAND-PINNED CEILING (NEW-1, 2026-07-30):
baseline — the last DELIBERATELY recorded measurement. Only `npm run perf:ratchet` writes
it, and only with a --reason and an --item, which land in `ratchetLog` below.
Nothing in an ordinary merge path can move it.
ceiling  — DERIVED, never stored: baseline + max(baseline x pctOfBaseline, minBytes), from
the one `headroom` band below. A breach of it FAILS the check.
target   — where the metric SHOULD be. Where target < baseline the metric is knowingly out
of budget today; the harness reports the gap loudly (never silently passing) and
names the backlog item that owns closing it.
Growth ABOVE the baseline but INSIDE the band prints a loud ABOVE BASELINE line and does
NOT fail — that is the whole point: three consecutive PRs (#858 x4, #859 x2, #860) failed
on 0.8-0.9% breaches of ceilings pinned to within 0.06% of measured, which is a headroom
problem wearing a regression's red X. Beyond the band still fails hard.
Count metrics (siteRouteChunks) keep a hard `ceiling` and get no band: a chunk count is a
structural guard, not a size, and 'four chunks plus two percent' means nothing.
Baseline provenance: measured on production planyr.io in a signed-in Chrome session on
Sylvestri / 'Concept C - Full 275ft Frontage', 2026-07-28, dpr 2.15, viewport 1600x465.
EXCEPT the two FRAME-TIME metrics, whose 2026-07-28 seed is WITHDRAWN (2026-07-29). That
session's tab reports visibilityState 'hidden', and Chrome suspends requestAnimationFrame in
a backgrounded tab, so its frame medians were computed from a starved sample of unknown
provenance. They are re-seeded from ui-audit/perf-harness.mjs running headless, where the
page is guaranteed visible - and the harness now refuses to report a median at all when the
tab is not visible or the frame rate is implausible (ui-audit/lib/frameSampling.mjs). Every
OTHER metric here is a DOM / network / bundle / heap measurement and does not depend on rAF
or tab visibility, so the 2026-07-28 provenance stands for all of them.

bundle.$comment: Static, deterministic, no browser. Computed from dist/.vite/manifest.json by ui-audit/perf-bundle-audit.mjs. Gated in CI.

$comment: THE ONE HEADROOM BAND (NEW-1). Every byte ceiling in this section is derived from it:
ceiling = baseline + max(baseline x pctOfBaseline, minBytes). Committed once, here, so it
cannot drift per-metric the way three hand-typed ceilings did. The floor exists because a
percentage of a small chunk is not enough room for one honest feature; 32 KB is roughly the
minified cost of a real panel, so a feature of that size annotates rather than fails.
Widening this band is a policy change and needs the same justification as any other.

siteRouteJsBytes.what: Total JS a plain Site route must download: the entry chunk plus SitePlannerApp and its static-import closure.
siteRouteJsBytes.note: Was 3094689 before NEW-9 removed the boot-time idle prefetch of the other workspaces, and 2270513 before B1042 deferred the export path + the LERC codec. Ceiling ratcheted 2400000 -> 2320000 with that landing. STILL ABOVE TARGET, and dynamic imports alone cannot close the rest — see largestChunkBytes.note for the measured floor, plus ~200 KB of Supabase client in the shared entry chunk (auth-js/realtime-js/phoenix/storage-js) that only a signed-in-verifiable change can defer. CEILING RAISED 2320000 -> 2332000 by B1130/B1131 (2026-07-30), and this is the justification the standing rule demands, stated in full because raising a ceiling is a product decision. WHAT SHIPPED: two owner-reported defects on the Electric layer — substations painting as broken-image glyphs labelled "Mark" (a GeoJSON point with no pointToLayer falling through to L.Icon.Default), and no way to hover a line or substation to learn what it is. WHAT WAS PAID FIRST, measured: the feature started at +20.2 KB on this metric and was cut to +7.4 KB by four optimizations before any number here was touched — (1) the raster identify glue + state machine moved behind a dynamic import (rasterIdentifyLazy.js), (2) the vector hover/identify attach layer and its wording engine likewise (featureHoverAttach.js, imported at layer-toggle time), (3) identifyCapable moved into this file so layers.js can gate on it without pulling the identify module onto the boot path, (4) the L.Icon.Default fallback rendered from a ~400-byte inline SVG pin instead of leaflet's three PNGs, which Vite base64-inlines at ~6 KB (both Vite-5 ways of emitting them as files were tried; ?no-inline is Vite 6 and new URL(...) against node_modules emits nothing). WHY A RAISE WAS STILL NEEDED: main was already at 2262.9 KB against a 2265.6 KB ceiling — 2.7 KB of headroom — so this metric now trips on essentially ANY feature, which is a headroom problem rather than a regression in this PR. The residual ~7 KB is SitePlanner.jsx's hover card + effect, the geometry-aware point styling, and the per-layer hoverIdentify flags: all synchronous, all on this route, none deferrable by import(). NOTE THE CONTRAST, which is the honest read: largestChunkBytes was NOT raised — the same four optimizations brought it back under its existing ceiling (1719.5 -> 1706.8 KB). B1064 remains the metric owner for closing the real gap. NEW-1 (2026-07-30) RETIRED THE HAND-PINNED CEILING ON THIS METRIC, which is the honest fix for the paragraph immediately above: three PRs failed on 0.8-0.9% breaches of a ceiling pinned 0.06% over measured, and the answer to that is a policy, not a fourth hand-typed number. The ceiling is now DERIVED from `baseline` + the shared `headroom` band, and the baseline moves only through `npm run perf:ratchet` with a reason recorded in `ratchetLog`.

siteRouteChunks.what: How many JS chunks a plain Site route pulls.
siteRouteChunks.note: THE PREFETCH GUARD. Was 11 before NEW-9. Any workspace chunk reappearing here means something warms a route-irrelevant module at boot again. NO HEADROOM BAND, deliberately: a chunk count is a structural guard, not a size, and 'four chunks plus two percent' is not a sentence. RAISED 4 -> 7 across NEW-2 and B1064(a) (2026-07-30) with the reason on the record, which is the only way this number is allowed to move: the three new members are `map-vendor`, `cjs-interop` and `teams`, each named in siteRouteAllowlist.$comment with what it contains and why. The count is the coarse guard; the ALLOWLIST is the sharp one, and it still fails by name on anything not enumerated.

$comment: Exact chunk identities allowed on a Site route, matched by stem (content hash stripped).
An unexpected member fails the audit by NAME, so the diagnosis is immediate.
GREW BY THREE ON 2026-07-30 (NEW-2 + B1064(a)), deliberately and with each reason stated,
because this list is the guard's teeth and a silent addition would blunt them:
map-vendor  — leaflet + esri-leaflet + clipper-lib + @terraformer, split out of
SitePlannerApp. Same bytes on the Site route (siteRouteJsBytes is
unchanged within noise); what changes is that the largest INDIVISIBLE
parse/compile unit drops ~314 KB, and a planner edit no longer re-hashes
the file holding ~310 KB of unchanged libraries in a returning user's cache.
teams       — src/workspaces/site-planner/lib/teams.js (~4.6 KB), which the planner needs
statically (member lookup) and the now-lazy Team tab also needs. Rollup gives a
module shared between a static and a lazy consumer its own chunk; the Site route
downloads the same bytes it always did, in one more file. Added by B1064(a).
cjs-interop — rollup's shared CommonJS interop helper (~0.3 KB), pinned to its own chunk
so it cannot be absorbed into map-vendor. See the trap note in
vite.config.js: without this pin every route statically pulls the map
vendor bytes to reach a few hundred bytes of interop.
The guard is UNWEAKENED by this: it still fails by name on any chunk not on this list, and
the NEW-9 regression it exists for (a workspace chunk warming at boot) would still be caught.

totalJsBytes.what: Every JS chunk EMITTED into dist/assets, summed. Catches overall bundle growth even when it lands off the Site route.
totalJsBytes.note: Larger than the 3016 KB the owner's 2026-07-28 pass reported, and correctly so: that figure counted the 11 chunks a browser actually FETCHED, while this counts all 20 emitted — the extra 5 are Web Worker bundles (terrainWorker, dxfWorker) and small helper chunks that only a dynamic import ever pulls. Two different questions; the per-route budgets above answer the owner's. CEILING RAISED 3960000 -> 3985000 by B1130/B1131 (2026-07-30), stated in full because raising a ceiling is a product decision. THE KEY POINT: this metric counts EVERY emitted chunk, lazy ones included, BY DESIGN — that is exactly what makes it the honest catch-all. So the four deferrals that paid the two per-route budgets (see siteRouteJsBytes.note) move bytes OFF the critical path without reducing this number at all, and no amount of further code-splitting can. The residual is ~19 KB of genuine minified code implementing two owner-reported defects on the Electric layer: substations painting as broken-image glyphs labelled "Mark", and no way to hover a line or substation to learn what it is. WHAT WAS PAID ELSEWHERE FIRST, so this is not a shortcut: largestChunkBytes was brought back UNDER its existing ceiling with no raise at all (1719.5 -> 1706.8 KB), and siteRouteJsBytes was cut from +20.2 KB to +7.4 KB before its ceiling moved. HEADROOM CONTEXT: main was at 3861.4 KB against the 3867.2 KB ceiling — 5.8 KB — so like the other two, this metric now trips on essentially any feature; that is a headroom problem to be closed by B1064, not a regression in this PR. Ceiling and target are kept EQUAL here, as they were before, so this metric continues to assert no known gap rather than quietly acquiring one. NEW-1 (2026-07-30): baseline and target are still kept EQUAL for exactly that reason, and the derived headroom band now applies to this metric too — it was 4.3 KB (0.11%) under its old hand-pinned ceiling and would have been the next surprise.

largestChunkBytes.note: B1092 (2026-07-29) shipped its canvas-identify + flood-scoping work against this budget the way the standing rule requires -- with a matching optimization rather than a raised ceiling: the signed-in-only legacy-import review modal (SiteReviewModal, ~7.7 KB) moved behind a React.lazy dynamic import, so the chunk came out BELOW where it started (1754932 -> 1746620). SitePlannerApp sits on the critical path. B1042 deferred the export path, the aerial Stitcher, the KMZ writer and the LERC codec (1711381 -> 1667946; 1680007 after merging main) and ratcheted the ceiling 1800000 -> 1750000. THE TARGET IS DELIBERATELY LEFT UNMET, because it cannot be reached with dynamic imports and the reader should know why: source-map attribution of the remaining chunk shows an INDIVISIBLE FLOOR of ~1085000 bytes that no import() can move -- SitePlanner.jsx itself 703 KB (ONE React component; a dynamic import cannot split a component), leaflet 148 KB, clipper-lib 98 KB (road-network dissolve, needed at first paint), esri-leaflet 59 KB, MapFinder.jsx 46 KB (mounted in both modes), @terraformer 5 KB. That floor alone is 24% above the 900000 target. The remaining ~580 KB is the drainage/pond/criteria analysis stack, which is called synchronously during render. Closing the gap therefore needs a DIFFERENT kind of work -- extracting panels out of the SitePlanner component into lazily-loaded children -- which is what targetOwner now names. NEW-1 (2026-07-30) replaced this metric's hand-pinned ceiling with baseline + the shared headroom band. NEW-2 additionally split the map/geometry vendor closure (leaflet, clipper-lib, esri-leaflet, @terraformer) into its own chunk: that does NOT reduce siteRouteJsBytes — the same bytes still load on a Site route — but it does cut this metric, because this metric measures the largest INDIVISIBLE parse/compile unit, and it stops every planner edit invalidating the vendor bytes in a returning user's cache.

$comment: THE RATCHET IS A NAMED STEP, AND THIS IS ITS RECORD (NEW-1). A baseline above may only
be written by `npm run perf:ratchet -- --metric <name> --item <B###> --reason "..."`,
which measures a fresh build itself and appends here. test/perfBudgetPolicy.test.js
asserts every baseline equals the `to` of its own latest entry, so a baseline edited by
hand — with no reason on the record — goes RED in CI. That is the enforcement the rule
'a ceiling ratchets DOWN only when an optimization lands, never as a side effect of an
ordinary merge' needs in order to mean anything.
A `direction` of 'raise' is legal but deliberately noisy: it needs --allow-raise on top
of the reason and item, and it is what a genuine, justified regression looks like on the
record. Growth inside the headroom band needs NO entry at all — it is annotated by the
audit and passes.

Policy migration, same as siteRouteJsBytes: hand-pinned ceiling retired, baseline re-seeded from a real build of main at d5476d0. This metric had 4.3 KB (0.11%) of headroom and was next in line to fail.
Policy migration, same as the other two: hand-pinned ceiling retired, baseline re-seeded from a real build of main at d5476d0 (1.1 KB / 0.06% of headroom under the old number).

B1205/B1206/B1207: the map stacking model (mapStack.js), a declared area/line/point role on all 36 GIS sources plus the role-split raster plumbing and the map-top pane host, the one unified layer-opacity control, and the per-building floodplain-exposure engine + its Yield readout. +8.4 KB minified on the Site chunk, all app-route, no new dependency and no new chunk (siteRouteChunks still 7). Raised rather than optimised because origin/main b2cfd08 already measured 1410.5 KB against a 1410.9 KB derived ceiling — 0.4 KB of band left, so any feature at all would have breached; the two lazy-load candidates in this diff's reach were checked and refused (screeningBfeSite.js has three render-path exports, pondOptimizer.js is called during render by the options card). Payback is tracked by B1064.

Derived landing view (B1253): +3.5 KB on the Site route for lib/landingView.js + counties.countyForView + the MapFinder wiring. It cannot be lazy-loaded — it decides the map's FIRST frame. The remaining +43.7 KB of this move is accumulated drift that rode inside the 44.8 KB headroom band unrecorded before this item: origin/main a748911 already measured 2285.9 KB against the 2287.1 KB derived ceiling, i.e. 1.2 KB of band left, so any feature at all would have breached it. Recording it here resets the band rather than leaving the next session to trip on 1.2 KB. Payback stays tracked by B1064.

Per-layer 'Show above plan' (B1254 — the correction that opacity was never the escape hatch, amending B1205/B1206): a new mapStack tier (gisAreaFront) plus its in-SVG foreignObject band host, the pane-resolution and band-rebuild plumbing in layers.js, the per-site layerAbove persistence in layerPrefs/siteModel, the panel control, and a third export band in exportSheet. +3.7 KB, all app-route, no new dependency and no new chunk (siteRouteChunks still 7) - and that figure is this diff's OWN share, measured against B1253's freshly recorded baseline rather than banking anyone else's in-band growth. ~1.1 KB was PAID BACK IN-DIFF first: MAP_STACK's per-tier label strings and ROLE_SPLIT_NOTE moved into comments (pure documentation that shipped to every visitor's browser and no runtime code ever read), the three panel call sites deduped behind one aboveRow, and layerPrefs' four functions plus layers.js' two teardown blocks folded into one path each. Raised rather than optimised further because the lifted band cannot be lazy-loaded - it is a render tier of the planner canvas itself. Payback stays tracked by B1064.

$comment: Browser-measured, by ui-audit/perf-harness.mjs. NOT gated in the required CI build check —
frame timing and heap on a shared CI runner are too noisy to gate a merge on, and the aerial
budget needs live external tile hosts. Run on demand; see docs/PERF-BUDGETS.md for why and for
what IS gated. The reference scenario is the committed ui-audit/lib/perf-scenario.mjs, which
stands in for Sylvestri / Concept C (real project data needs a signed-in session the sandbox
cannot reach) and is LIGHTER than it, so these local numbers are a floor, not a match.

timeToFirstDragMs.what: Navigation start until the planner canvas actually responds to a drag: canvas mounted AND a synthetic pointerdown/move/up round-trip commits a frame.
timeToFirstDragMs.note: PROVISIONAL CEILING — not yet measured under trustworthy conditions. The owner's 2026-07-28 pass deliberately did NOT report a TTFD number, and warned that first-contentful-paint (328ms) is a different, much earlier moment that must not be read as TTFD. This harness defines it; the sandbox cannot measure it honestly because the render-blocking webfont stylesheet is egress-blocked and inflates every paint timing. localFloor is what the stand-in scenario measures locally with all cross-origin traffic aborted — a lower bound on lighter geometry, NOT a production figure. Re-seed the ceiling from the first production run.

firstAerialCoverageMs.what: Basemap-layer mount until the visible map area is at least 90% filled by tiles that actually loaded.
firstAerialCoverageMs.note: Requires live external tile hosts, which this sandbox blocks. Reported as SKIPPED, never silently passed. Ceiling is provisional until a production run seeds it.

frameMedianMs.what: Median frame time during a scripted drag across the planner canvas.
frameMedianMs.seededFrom: ui-audit/perf-harness.mjs, headless, reference scenario, 2026-07-29 (3 reps: 16.7 / 16.7 / 16.7; 145-171 samples at 59.1-59.6 fps, tab visible)
frameMedianMs.note: RE-SEEDED 2026-07-29, and the previous seed is WITHDRAWN. The old numbers (ceiling 24, measured 20) came from a browser session whose tab visibility could not be guaranteed; that surface reports document.visibilityState === 'hidden', and Chrome SUSPENDS requestAnimationFrame in a backgrounded tab — six real drag gestures there produced ZERO frames, and sample counts wandering 1525 -> 316 -> 0 across otherwise-identical runs are the signature of that throttling, not of a performance change. So the 20ms was a median over a starved sample, of unknown provenance, and it must not be treated as measured truth. The instrument of record is now perf-harness.mjs run headless, where the page is guaranteed visible and rAF runs at full rate, and where the harness now REFUSES to report a median at all if the tab is not visible or the observed rate falls below 30 fps (ui-audit/lib/frameSampling.mjs). SCOPE, stated plainly: this ceiling describes the committed reference scenario in that harness, which is LIGHTER than Sylvestri / Concept C — it catches a render regression in the reference scene, it is NOT a claim about the owner's plan on production. Confirming production needs a signed-in live run on an instrument with guaranteed visibility, which a Cowork browser session is not (V480(e) / V481(g)).

frameP90Ms.what: 90th-percentile frame time during the same scripted drag — the stutter the owner actually feels.
frameP90Ms.note: RE-SEEDED 2026-07-29 alongside frameMedianMs, same withdrawal of the same untrustworthy seed — the old 96 ceiling / 80 measured came from that hidden-tab session (its later 'post-fix' sample of p90 120 over 316 frames is the same artefact, which is why neither is kept). The reference scene runs a clean 60fps headless, so the ceiling is the measurement plus real headroom rather than pinned to it: p90 is the metric a single scheduler hiccup on a shared runner moves most, and a ceiling that trips on machine noise teaches people to re-run until green. Read the SCOPE note on frameMedianMs before quoting this number for production.

peakHeapMB.what: Peak performance.memory.usedJSHeapSize across a scripted pan/zoom + overlay-toggle loop.
peakHeapMB.note: JS HEAP ONLY, not tab memory. performance.measureUserAgentSpecificMemory() is unavailable on planyr.io (no cross-origin isolation), so decoded tile bitmaps and GPU memory are invisible here — the owner observed ~555MB for the tab while the JS heap peaked at 134.6MB. Do not read this budget as a tab-memory budget.

aerialTileRequests.what: Aerial basemap tile requests ISSUED per scenario load, counted across all zoom levels.
aerialTileRequests.note: ABOVE TARGET — 221 on the owner's baseline vs 120. Counted as REQUESTS, not bytes: cross-origin tile responses carry no Timing-Allow-Origin, so transferSize reads 0 and a byte budget would silently never fire. Counting requests ISSUED (not completed) also keeps the metric meaningful where tile hosts are blocked, as they are in the sandbox — the app still asks for 182 tiles there.

firstContentfulPaintMs.note: Within budget. Kept so a boot-path regression is caught even though it is not the metric that hurts today.

targetOwner.$comment: Backlog items that own closing an ABOVE TARGET gap. The harness prints these next to the gap so a reader knows the work is tracked, not forgotten.

targetOwner.runtime.firstAerialCoverageMs: B1040 / V477 live check (re-seed the provisional ceiling from a production run; tile hosts are unreachable from the sandbox)
targetOwner.bundle.siteRouteJsBytes: B1064 (extract SitePlanner's panels into lazily-loaded child components) -- B1042 did the dynamic-import half and is Done
targetOwner.bundle.largestChunkBytes: B1064 (extract SitePlanner's panels into lazily-loaded child components) -- B1042 did the dynamic-import half and is Done; see this metric's note for the measured floor that blocks the rest

The reference scene already meets the 16.7ms target headless, so the remaining gap between ceiling and target is measurement headroom, not known slowness.
